mutations.contract: Deselecting a face puts its colours back. The pick state and the orange in the colour buffer are ONE fact, and the bug this closed was exactly them disagreeing.
mutations.note: Jeff: "I accidentally clicked a face ... but there's no way to deselect a surface." The mutation restores the pre-handoff behaviour precisely -- forget the pick, leave the tint -- which is invisible to everything except a real GL context, so this entry can only be owned by the browser tier. `window.__scene.highlightedFace()` is the observable it reads. This entry earned its keep immediately: the first version of the guard read `scene.highlightedFace()`, which reports `_lastPick` -- the BOOKKEEPING -- so the mutation cleared the flag, left the mesh orange, and the check stayed green. It reads the live colour attribute against `userData.baseColors` now, which is the claim.
